note.title: Creating Content with HTML
steps: Use `<h1>` to `<h6>` for headings, from the main title to less important subheadings.
Create a link with `link text`.
Add an image with ``.
Use `<ul>` for a bulleted list or `<ol>` for a numbered list, with each item inside `<li>` tags.
Create a table with `<table>`, rows with `<tr>`, headings with `<th>`, and data cells with `<td>`. Comments go between `<!--` and `-->`.
note.answer: HTML content is the information on a web page that users read and interact with, such as text, images, videos, links, and other elements.

mcqs.stem: Which code correctly creates a link to another web page?
rationales: Correct: The `<a>` tag creates the link, and `href` gives its address.
Incorrect: `<link>` is not the link syntax shown for clickable page content.
Incorrect: `href` is an attribute, not an HTML tag.

mcqs.stem: Which code adds an image and provides alternate text?
rationales: Correct: `` adds the image, while `src` and `alt` provide its file and description.
Incorrect: The section uses ``, not ``, and `href` is used for links.

mcqs.stem: Which tag creates a numbered list?
rationales: Incorrect: `<ul>` creates a bulleted list.
Correct: `<ol>` creates an ordered, numbered list.
Incorrect: `<li>` marks an item inside a list.
Incorrect: `<table>` creates a table.

mcqs.stem: Which tag defines a row in an HTML table?
rationales: Incorrect: `<td>` defines a data cell in a row.
Incorrect: `<th>` defines a table heading cell.
Correct: `<tr>` defines a table row.
Incorrect: `<table>` creates the table itself, not an individual row.

mcqs.stem: Which syntax creates an HTML comment that is not rendered by the browser?
rationales: Correct: HTML comments begin with `<!--` and end with `-->`.
Incorrect: `//` is not the HTML comment syntax in this section.
Incorrect: `/* ... */` is not the HTML comment syntax in this section.
Incorrect: `<comment>` is not the comment syntax shown for HTML.

explain.title: Headings show content hierarchy
explain.body: Headings in HTML, ranging from `<h1>` to `<h6>`, are used to define the structure and hierarchy of content on a web page. Use `<h1>` for the main title and lower levels for subheadings. This helps organize content and helps search engines understand the page.

explain.title: Paragraphs separate text
explain.body:
Paragraphs in HTML are used to organize and separate text into readable sections. Each paragraph creates a block of text with space above and below it, making the content easier to read. Paragraphs starts with the `

` tag and it ends with `

`.

explain.title: Links connect pages
explain.body: Links in HTML are used to connect one web page to another. They are created using the `<a>` tag. The `href` attribute gives the destination. A `mailto:` link opens an email program.

explain.title: Images need useful alternate text
explain.body: Images are added using the `` tag. The `src` attribute identifies the image file, and `alt` provides alternate text so visually impaired users can understand what the image represents.

explain.title: Lists and tables organize information
explain.body: Use `<ul>` for an unordered, bulleted list and `<ol>` for an ordered, numbered list. Both use `<li>` for list items. A table uses `<table>` to contain `<tr>` rows, `<th>` headings, and `<td>` data cells.

explain.title: Comments are not displayed
explain.body: HTML comments begin with `<!--` and end with `-->`. Text inside these markers is treated as a comment and is not rendered by the browser.

mistakes: Using `<ul>` when a numbered list is needed, or `<ol>` when a bulleted list is needed.

Leaving out a closing tag such as `

` or `` when the element requires one.
Putting a link destination outside the `href` attribute or forgetting the clickable link text.
Adding an image without the `src` attribute or useful `alt` text.
Mixing up table rows and cells: `<tr>` is a row, `<th>` is a heading cell, and `<td>` is a data cell.
Writing an HTML comment with the wrong markers or expecting its text to appear on the page.
